nodes.description: The only intervention shown to change survival, and a contested one. The 2024 international cohort found transplantation significantly improved survival in 26 patients and, unlike earlier analyses, found no survival difference by presence of neurological involvement overall, though nystagmus at onset predicted worse post-transplant survival. A 2008 review concluded that profound hypotonia, psychomotor retardation or nystagmus make transplantation futile; GeneReviews limits it to children without, or with minimal, neurological involvement. About half of transplanted children in a separate collation died within two years, and neurological or muscle disease can emerge afterwards. Pulmonary hypertension was the most frequent cause of death after transplantation in the 2024 cohort (4 of 13 post-transplant deaths), which is relevant to post-transplant follow-up.

evidence.snippet: mtDNA copy number was measured in DNA extracted from muscle biopsy samples in 30/202. Depletion was found in 20/30 (66.7%)

evidence.reference_title: Deoxyguanosine kinase deficiency: natural history and liver transplant outcome.
evidence.snippet: Histochemical analysis of muscle biopsy showed cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficient muscular fibres in 19/45 (42.2%) patients

nodes.description: Intragenic deletion carried by all three Japanese DGUOK-deficient patients in a national series.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular basis of hepatocerebral mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome in Japan: evaluation of outcomes after liver transplantation.
evidence.snippet: Eight MPV17-deficient patients harbored c.451dupC and all three DGUOK-deficient patients harbored c.143-307_170del335.

nodes.description: The most frequently reported allele in the 2008 series, seen in eight unrelated kindreds.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular features of mitochondrial DNA depletion due to mutations in deoxyguanosine kinase.
evidence.snippet: The most frequent mutation, c.763_c.766dupGATT, occurs in 8 unrelated kindreds.

nodes.description: Reduced mtDNA; used to test purine nucleoside supplementation.
Missense allele with residual activity, found in a revertant hepatic case in trans with L266R and homozygous in noncirrhotic portal hypertension 1.

evidence.reference_title: Kinetic properties of mutant deoxyguanosine kinase in a case of reversible hepatic mtDNA depletion.
evidence.snippet: The N46S/L266R DGUOK showed 14 and 10% residual activity as compared with controls with dG and deoxyadenosine as phosphate acceptors respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent recessive mutation in deoxyguanosine kinase causes idiopathic noncirrhotic portal hypertension.
evidence.snippet: Three subjects from two consanguineous families shared the identical rare homozygous p.N46S mutation in DGUOK, a deoxyguanosine kinase required for mitochondrial DNA replication
